Start with the plain-language section. Use the source tables at the bottom only when you need a link or a date.

## In plain language

Hong Kong is trying to build a **low-altitude economy**: flying tasks such as inspection, delivery and, later, other services, generally below 1,000 metres. This page records what the government has actually decided. It is not a market forecast.

### Who is in charge?

A **Working Group**, led by the Deputy Financial Secretary, coordinates policy. The **Civil Aviation Department** enforces the Small Unmanned Aircraft Order (Cap. 448G), the main Hong Kong law for drones. A full **Action Plan** has been promised; the text is not published yet.

### Two different trial schemes

**Regulatory Sandbox** (first cohort). Industry and public bodies proposed 72 projects. The government selected **38** on 20 March 2025. These are supervised trials, not an open market. Beyond-visual-line-of-sight flying in this scheme follows Civil Aviation Department circular AC-013.

**Regulatory Sandbox X** is a later, harder scheme (announced November 2025). It covers more complex tests, including traffic-management demonstrations and possible cross-boundary flights. Circular AC-017 covers cross-boundary trials inside Sandbox X. Results of those cross-boundary trials have **not** been published.

Do not add 38 to the Sandbox X module counts. They are not the same programme.

### Radio spectrum

From 27 October 2025, a dedicated band (**1430–1444 MHz**) can be licensed for Sandbox projects. It is not a general public mobile band.

### The HK$350 billion figure

Our Hong Kong Foundation, a think tank, projected about **HK$350 billion** of **industry value-added in Hong Kong by 2050**. That is not a government forecast and not this year’s output. If you use the number, name the Foundation, the metric, the place, and the year 2050.

### Mainland rules, in one paragraph

Unmanned-aircraft operations on the Mainland still rest on the 2024 State Council rules and CCAR-92. A revised Civil Aviation Law took effect on **1 July 2026**. A 2026 draft on air-traffic rules (Chapter 12) is only a consultation text.

### Greater Bay Area

Guangdong has a published policy target. Shenzhen has run **domestic** medical-sample flights. An **operating** Shenzhen–Hong Kong medical drone corridor is **not** documented. Officials have described it as planned or on trial under Sandbox X.

### What you still must not write

Do not write that the government estimates HK$350 billion. Do not invent a Hong Kong vertiport statute, a published Action Plan, or a completed cross-boundary corridor.

## Mainland rules

For operations today, cite 国令761 and CCAR-92. The 2025 Civil Aviation Law is in force from 1 July 2026; the ATM Chapter 12 text is still a draft.

| [CAAC ATM Rules (征求意见稿) — Ch.12 UAS](https://www.caac.gov.cn/HDJL/YJZJ/202608/t20260811_231462.html) | **Draft** **2026-08-11** (comments to **2026-09-11**); CAAC; **not** promulgated; not Art.34/225 decree | T1 |

Ops today: cite **761 + CCAR-92**. Law Art. 258 defers UAS rules to State Council/CMC.

CAAC ATM Rules draft is under consultation through **2026-09-11**. Do not treat as effective law.
